title: Majestic Residence: a dual-key block built purely for returns.
videoTitle: PROPERTY REVIEW #414 | MAJESTIC RESIDENCE, KL CITY CENTER
excerpt: A compact block behind Quill City Mall designed for short stays and dual-key letting. Sean admires its multiple rental options and efficient design, but warns of a cramped setting and coming competition.
takeaways: A 654 sq ft dual-key unit lists at about RM650,000 and its two halves ask about RM3,000 to RM3,200 each.
Designed for investors: double-loaded corridors, a rooftop infinity pool and a combined gym and work lounge.
A cramped site beside a substation, a mall loading bay and a temporary poultry slaughterhouse.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: Majestic Residence is built for investors and short-stay guests: QR-code access, 20 units a floor along double-loaded corridors served by four lifts, the lift core and air-conditioner compressors tucked into one corner, and a rooftop with a lap pool and infinity edge facing KLCC, a lounge, and a glass-walled gym combined with phone booths, meeting spaces and a games room.

Units come in 450 sq ft and 654 sq ft. Sean viewed a 654 sq ft unit set up as a dual key: two studio-like halves, each 3.3 m wide with a 2.9 m ceiling, its own bathroom and a pantry on the shared wall, with near full-height tinted windows. Owners can keep it whole or let each half separately.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: The block sits off the junction of Jalan Sultan Ismail and Jalan Tuanku Abdul Rahman, a short walk from Quill City Mall, which connects to the monorail; the LRT is a little further. Offices, hotels, Kampung Baru and Raja Uda's eateries, the old town's traditional restaurants and KLCC and Pavilion are all within reach. A TNB substation stands in front, and the site sits on a narrow dead end beside old buildings and empty plots awaiting development.

sections.heading: Rent and returns
paragraphs: Listings ask about RM650,000 for a 654 sq ft unit, about RM1,000 psf. Each half of a dual-key unit asks about RM3,000 to RM3,200 a month, about RM5,200 together, which Sean reckons is roughly a 9% to 10% return. He calls 6% from long-term letting solid, but warns that short-stay returns of 18% to 20% are seasonal and fall when newer buildings open.

standout.title: One unit, many ways to let it
standout.body: Water points and sockets sit on the wall shared by the two halves, so the same 654 sq ft unit can be one home, a dual key let room by room, a short-stay pair or beds for students. Sean calls this multiple rental option the best test of an investment unit, though furnishing it costs double.

pros: The location at the junction of Jalan Sultan Ismail and Jalan Tuanku Abdul Rahman, mixing the old town's food and Kampung Baru's street stalls with KLCC and Pavilion nearby, plus the monorail.
Multiple rental options: long-term, medium-term, room by room, by the bed or short stay, with tenants from offices, tourism and colleges, at returns he estimates at 9% to 10%.

Design with clear intent: an efficient, no-frills building that puts negative spaces in one corner, a comfortable 3.3 m unit width, utilities placed for dual-key use, big windows and a rooftop that wins guests on booking platforms.
cons: The immediate setting: narrow roads and junctions, a substation in front, a dead end, the mall's busy loading bay, illegal parking, loud music from old buildings behind and a temporary poultry slaughterhouse next door.
Competition: many KLCC-area projects are chasing the same short-stay market and privately owned land nearby will bring more, so don't count on peak Airbnb returns lasting.

It isn't for family living: a one-way drop-off, deliveries through the lobby with no service lift from the loading bay, long walks from the corner lift core, and a building with no architectural ambition.

closing: A pure investment product that keeps owners, tenants and the developer happy, as long as you don't buy it to raise a family.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this November 2025 episode and its video description. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. An owner let Sean view the unit after completion; prices and rents are from listings as he quoted them, and the returns are his estimates. The Makeover Guys, where Sean works, appear to have furnished the unit.
